answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable stake: each agent must lock a bond before its vote counts, and double-voting burns the whole bond. Think of a wharf where every ship pays a docking deposit and a vessel caught cheating forfeits it. A plume of fake identities then costs a fresh bond per fake, so the attacker's capital outlay grows with every fake name while any single vote pays far less. With bonds as unforgiving as basalt, flooding a majority costs more than the prize, making the attack irrational.
